name: Deep Learning 9 — Practice Lab (Batch Normalization, CNN Building Blocks and Residual Connections)
description: Guided learner workspace for the ninth lab of a Deep Learning course (v1.0, run in Google Colab or local Jupyter) on batch normalization, CNN building blocks and residual connections, closing with a controlled two-model comparison on CIFAR-10. On the Inno Agent side an explanatory tutor works: the learner runs the cells of their own notebook one at a time (PTE_DL9_CNN_LAB.ipynb, 28 points in the order fixed by CELLA_TERKEP.json: E01 environment and GPU gate, B01–B06 batch normalization from the sample/feature panel through gamma–beta, real Keras weights and moving statistics to the frozen BN and the link back to lesson 8, P01–P02 local and global pooling and the flatten versus GAP head parameter count, C01 the 1×1 convolution, R00 observation on the skip-connection demo, R01–R03 the real residual block, the projection shortcut and the gradient probe, G01–G02 dropout and L2 regularization, D01–D03 CIFAR-10 images, the fixed 8000/2000/2000 split (800/200/200 per class) and the shared batches, M01–M05 two small CNNs from one builder (5370 versus 5562 parameters, identical layer order and batches, six epochs each with a separate Adam 1e-3), restored best val_loss checkpoints and the validation-based decision, V01 the final test only after that decision on the fixed 2000 images, V02 step-by-step estimates and the 10×10 confusion matrix, Z01–Z02 three short reflections and the closing summary). Three points are discussion only (B01, R00, Z01); the other 25 are code cells. The two interactive explanations ship unchanged as HTML under forrasok/. The learner writes no code and is never asked for the notebook, a submission or a saved artifact; no homework and no extra task.
